title: Billing Runway Triage Workbook
summary: Working worksheet for QBRs focused on short-term billing runway diagnostics and customer-facing remediation plans. Designed to be fast to fill during a 30–60 minute internal triage and editable live in a customer-facing QBR meeting.
primary_objectives: Quickly determine if current spend trajectory exceeds committed budget or renewal expectations
Identify imminent rate-limit or quota risks and propose immediate mitigations
Produce a 3-action remediation plan to present in QBR and hand off to engineering/AE
diagnostic_checklist: 1) Confirm billing window and billing cadence (monthly/annual) + committed spend vs actual to date
2) Compute 7/14/30 day token burn rate and extrapolate 30/60 day runway
3) Identify top 10 API keys by spend and % of total (include service accounts and internal integrations)
4) Check for recent spikes correlated to deployments, marketing campaigns, or customer growth events
5) Look for repeated rate-limit responses (HTTP 429 patterns) and map to clients/routes
6) Validate any recent quota increases, overruns, or corrective tickets (billing, infra, or AE requests)
7) Flag long-tail low-velocity calls that cumulatively drive cost (e.g., high-context embedding pipelines)
key_metrics_table:
Columns: metric | last 7d | last 30d | projected 30d | notes
- total_tokens | 1.2M | 4.9M | 6.6M | spike on 2025-02-26
- billable_calls | 44k | 160k | 210k | 70% chat, 30% embeddings
- top_key_pct | 42% | 45% | 48% | key AK-23 accounts for bulk of burst
- avg_cost_per_1k_tokens | $0.95 | $0.92 | $0.93 | quantized variants in prod reduce cost in upper bound
spend_signals_and_thresholds: Green: projection shows <80% of committed budget in next 30 days
Yellow: projection 80%–100% of committed budget in next 30 days -> recommend budget alert + rate-limit guidance
Red: projection >100% of committed budget in next 30 days -> immediate AE notification, propose throttles / canary fallback
rate_limit_investigation_steps: Collect all 429 timestamps and map to client IDs + routes
Overlay with latency and error rates to see if 429s are contention-related or throttles from our side
Check autoscale/burst config for Dedicated customers and verify effective throughput limits
If 429s coincide with large embedding jobs, surface as candidate for batching optimization or background workqueue
recommended_quick_mitigations: Temporary per-key throttles (soft cap) with notification to the customer
Enable caching of frequent prompts / embedding vectors for 48–72 hrs
Suggest downgraded model variant with cost-inference tradeoff for non-latency-critical paths
Apply request sampling and quota windows (e.g., 1 request per 5s for identified endpoints)
3_action_qbr_plan_template: Action 1: Short-term throttle + alerting — set soft caps for top keys, AE to notify customer within 24 hours
Action 2: Optimize pipeline — run embedding dedupe and enable caching; target 20–30% token reduction in 2 weeks
Action 3: Renewal/commit sync — propose adjusted committed capacity or temporary overage buffer; ops to deliver cost estimate by next week
escalation_playbook: Owner: CS Manager -> triage lead (within 4 hours)
If projected overrun >25% and customer is enterprise, escalate to AE + Solutions Eng and schedule 1:1
If repeated 429s persist after mitigations, open SRE ticket with priority P1 and include sample traces and kv-cache metrics
qbr_talking_points: 1. Current runway and projection in simple visual (green/yellow/red)
2. Top drivers of spend (feature, route, or campaign) and proposed mitigations
3. Customer impact: latency, error surface, and business risk
4. Proposed contractual options (temporary buffer, commit adjustment, or rate-limit changes)
5. Next steps and owner commitments with dates
noted_unknowns_and_followups: - Need confirm from infra whether a recent kernel upgrade changed token counting semantics (ticket INF-412)
- Validate whether third-party pipeline (vendor X) started backfilling historical embeddings on 2025-02-25
- Confirm whether marketing campaign 'Spring Sync' was live Feb 22–28 (possible traffic deltas)
sample_queries_and_snippets:
-- Top keys by spend (BigQuery)
SELECT api_key, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SUM(cost) as cost FROM billing.events WHERE event_time BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY api_key ORDER BY cost DESC LIMIT 20;

-- 429 sample extraction
SELECT request_id, api_key, route, status, timestamp FROM logs.requests WHERE status = 429 AND timestamp >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY) ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 200;

-- 30-day runway projection (simple rate)
WITH last30 AS (SELECT SUM(tokens) as tokens FROM billing.events WHERE event_time >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 30 DAY)) SELECT tokens, (tokens / 30) * 60 AS projected_60d FROM last30;
presentation_notes_for_cs: Keep language non-technical for execs; for engineering stakeholders include the two SQL snippets above and a short list of infra artefacts (traces, kv-cache hit rate). Use the 3-action plan as the QBR take-away and assign dates.
final_checklist_before_qbr: Populate metrics table and attach last 30 days CSV
Confirm AE has reached out if projection is Yellow/Red
Prepare one-sentence ask (e.g., "request temporary 15% overage buffer")
Attach linked tickets and ownership rows
